# Jubilees Chapter 29 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob departs from Laban; wrestling at Peniel

---

**29:1** In the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Jacob went to Laban to take his leave and return to his father in the land of Canaan.

**29:2** Laban called together all his flocks, all his sons, and all his daughters, and embraced and kissed Jacob and wept greatly. He said to Jacob: "Please do not leave me. You have found favor in my sight. Stay with me, and God will bless me for your sake."

**29:3** But Jacob would not stay and said to Laban: "Let me go; my father and mother are waiting for me. Release me so I may go."

**29:4** Laban took his leave of him with weeping, and Jacob went on his way.

**29:5** Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir.

**29:6** They returned to Jacob with the report: "We went to your brother Esau, and he is coming to meet you with four hundred men."

**29:7** Jacob was greatly afraid. He divided the people with him, the flocks, the herds, and the camels into two groups,

**29:8** Thinking: "If Esau comes and attacks one group, the remaining group will be able to escape."

**29:9** Jacob prayed to the LORD his God: "O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O LORD, who said to me: 'Return to your land and to your kindred, and I will deal well with you' —

**29:10** I am unworthy of all the steadfast love and faithfulness you have shown your servant, for with only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.

**29:11** Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid of him — afraid that he will come and attack me, the mothers together with the children.

**29:12** Yet you said: 'I will surely do you good and make your descendants as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered.'"

**29:13** Jacob stayed there that night and set aside a gift for his brother Esau from what he had with him: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams, thirty milking camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.

**29:14** He put them in separate herds in his servants' care, with intervals between drove and drove.

**29:15** He instructed the lead servant: "When my brother Esau meets you and asks: 'To whom do you belong? Where are you going? And whose animals are these?' —

**29:16** Say: 'They belong to your servant Jacob; they are a gift sent to my lord Esau; and he himself is also coming behind us.'"

**29:17** Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until the breaking of day.

**29:18** When the man saw that he could not overpower him, he struck the socket of Jacob's hip, and the socket of Jacob's hip was wrenched as they wrestled.

**29:19** The man said: "Let me go, for the day is breaking." Jacob said: "I will not let you go unless you bless me."

**29:20** He said: "What is your name?" He said: "Jacob." He said: "Your name shall no longer be called Jacob but Israel; for you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed."

**29:21** Jacob asked: "Tell me your name, I pray." He said: "Why do you ask my name?" And he blessed him there.

**29:22** Jacob named the place Peniel, saying: "I have seen God face to face, and yet I am alive."

**29:23** The sun rose upon him as he passed over Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.

**29:24** Therefore the children of Israel do not eat the sinew of the hip that is at the socket of the hip, to this day.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering following LOGOS throughout with minor EMET influences in the prayer (vv.9-12). "Steadfast love and faithfulness" renders the Ge'ez compound for hesed-ve-emet, following established project convention. The wrestling episode is rendered in the formal register appropriate to its theological weight.*
